head.citation-title: Microstructure characteristics and evolution of pipe pile concrete under centrifugation and steam curing
head.abstracts: © 2024 Elsevier LtdPrestressed high-strength concrete (PHC) pipe piles have become an important part of modern civil engineering projects, providing excellent load carrying capacity and structural integrity. However, the current study neglects the microstructural differences along the radial aspect brought about by the special manufacturing method (centrifugation, stream curing) of PHC piles. This microstructural is critical to the macroscopic properties of pipe pile concrete. In this paper, the microstructure evolution and hydration products of different PHC pipe piles position were researched. The results show that the tetrahedral bond angle, polymerization degree and Ca/Si in the middle position of the pipe pile concrete were higher than those in the inner and outer sides. The hydration degree of different pipe pile position is different. The pore content on the inside of the pipe pile were much larger than that on the outside at the early stage of hydration. The morphology of the different layers was obviously different from BSE images. At the age of 4–8 h, the outer side of the pipe pile concrete contained more ettringite than the other concrete layers. The water loss rate increases, and the w/b decreases as the pipe pile from the outside to the inside. The results provide further insights into the microstructure, corrosion resistance and durability design of pipe pile concrete.

coredata.dc:description: Prestressed high-strength concrete (PHC) pipe piles have become an important part of modern civil engineering projects, providing excellent load carrying capacity and structural integrity. However, the current study neglects the microstructural differences along the radial aspect brought about by the special manufacturing method (centrifugation, stream curing) of PHC piles. This microstructural is critical to the macroscopic properties of pipe pile concrete. In this paper, the microstructure evolution and hydration products of different PHC pipe piles position were researched. The results show that the tetrahedral bond angle, polymerization degree and Ca/Si in the middle position of the pipe pile concrete were higher than those in the inner and outer sides. The hydration degree of different pipe pile position is different. The pore content on the inside of the pipe pile were much larger than that on the outside at the early stage of hydration. The morphology of the different layers was obviously different from BSE images. At the age of 4–8 h, the outer side of the pipe pile concrete contained more ettringite than the other concrete layers. The water loss rate increases, and the w/b decreases as the pipe pile from the outside to the inside. The results provide further insights into the microstructure, corrosion resistance and durability design of pipe pile concrete.
coredata.dc:title: Microstructure characteristics and evolution of pipe pile concrete under centrifugation and steam curing
